name: 3Commas
summary: Mature multi-exchange bot platform (founded 2017) with DCA, grid and TradingView-webhook signal bots, SmartTrade terminal for complex SL/TP, and a $10,000 virtual demo account. Subscription $20–140/month. Its signal bots and SmartTrade risk controls are the closest commercial parallel to this app.

name: Pionex
summary: Exchange with 16+ built-in bots (grid, DCA, reverse grid, arbitrage) — zero API-key sharing because funds stay on the venue; 0.05% spot fee, no bot subscription. Shows how strong 'no external key exposure' is as a safety story.

name: Cryptohopper
summary: Indicator strategy designer + signal marketplace with paper trading (one paper bot per tier) and a panic button that closes positions. Pricing $29–129/month. Marketplace signals are its moat; rent-a-strategy performance risk is its weakness.

name: Bitsgap
summary: Grid/DCA/futures bots across 17 exchanges with $100,000 demo accounts, backtesting per plan tier, and an AI assistant that proposes grid configurations. API keys must be trading-only — withdrawals enabled keys are rejected.
borrowed: trade-only API key enforcement (documented in Settings)

name: Open-source Binance bots (volatility bot & TradingView webhook bots)
summary: Popular GitHub bots add the operational patterns: risk checks in order (allowlist → size cap → per-symbol cap → total exposure → daily loss halt → cooldown), dry-run mode, idempotent orders, and 'exit immediately on SL, never wait for confirmation'. The Binance volatility bot scans every USDT pair for momentum spikes.

name: AI multi-agent trading bots
summary: Newer bots layer LLM 'AI committees' that must approve entries at a confidence threshold, while stop-loss/trailing exits stay 100% mechanical. Also fee-aware take-profits that ignore signals which don't cover round-trip fees.
borrowed: fee-adjusted TP (0.1% taker in our math)
